handoff.summary: Batch b12: genotype-frequency-from-counts r2 renaming two misleading reference IDs.
gaps: No new quantity meanings, references, or model IDs in this batch; prior batches' deferred items stand unchanged.
handoff.review_notes: Correction-style batch, single r2 record. Change: reference IDs 'yy-class-frequency' and 'yy-class-heterozygote' renamed to 'dominant-homozygote-frequency' and 'heterozygote-frequency' because the data are YY (245) and Yy (210) class counts, not yy. Found during the curator's full-prose review pass. No review corrections were supplied. Validate bundle and packed ZIP.

assumptions: source assumption: the census counts every individual of the sampled population exactly once, so class counts sum to the census total N.
source assumption: the frequency is a within-sample proportion at one survey time; no equilibrium or time-dynamics meaning is attached (contrast the Hardy-Weinberg prediction records).

gaps: Quantity meanings genotype_count, individual_count and genotype_frequency are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot; runtime projection omitted.

models.inverse_notes: Class count is recoverable as n = f*N for a known census total. Substitution check: 0.49*500 = 245, consistent with the YY reference. N = 0 is excluded (a proportion over an empty census is undefined); the zero-count boundary n = 0 gives f = 0 and is admissible.
limitations: A pure accounting proportion; it estimates no equilibrium and must not be confused with the Hardy-Weinberg predicted frequency, against which it is compared.
Requires complete, non-overlapping classification; unsampled individuals are outside its scope.

references.method: Figure 19.2 extended description: 245 YY of 500 individuals (245/500 = 0.49); proportion recomputed from the printed counts, matching the printed .49.
references.provenance: Value derived independently from published figure counts (not the printed proportion).

references.method: Figure 19.2 extended description: 210 Yy of 500 individuals (210/500 = 0.42); proportion recomputed from the printed counts, matching the printed .42.
references.provenance: Value derived independently from published figure counts (not the printed proportion).

rejection_cases.reason: A class count (600) cannot exceed the census total (500) in one complete non-overlapping census.
Census total N is required; a bare class count is not a frequency.

relationship.locator: Section 19.1 Figure 19.2 extended description: genotype frequencies stated alongside counts out of 500 individuals (YY .49 with 245, Yy .42 with 210, yy .09 with 45); allele-frequency subsection defines frequency as copies divided by total copies, applied here to individuals.
relationship.original_equation: genotype frequency = class count divided by census total
relationship.translation_notes: Accounting proportion formalized from the figure's count-to-frequency pairing; symbols n and N are introduced. Dimensional check: count divided by count gives a dimensionless frequency.

sources.evidence: Paraphrase: Figure 19.2 pairs each genotype count with its frequency (245/500 -> .49, 210/500 -> .42, 45/500 -> .09); frequency defined as part divided by total.

models.summary: Accounting definition of an observed genotype frequency as class count over census total. r2 renames two reference IDs that misleadingly used lowercase 'yy' for YY/Yy class data.
models.title: Genotype frequency from observed class counts
